author: delegate-gp[bot]
title: fix: fulfil Pro from customer.subscription.created and stamp userId/campaignId on the subscription (ENG-11182, ENG-11672)
body:
`campaign.details.subscriptionId` is the only mapping from a Stripe subscription back to an account, and one webhook wrote it. A `checkout.session.completed` that is missed, delayed or lost leaves a paying account on the free plan with nothing to retry, no local record of what to retry, and no way out except a human cancelling in Stripe. That is the shape of [ENG-11672](https://app.clickup.com/t/86a9x9mv5) and of the class ticket [ENG-11182](https://app.clickup.com/t/86a9x9c8c); the root-cause analysis and the ranked fix set are at https://billing-account-link-rca.artifacts.goodparty.org.

This is the P1 from that analysis: make the second arm of Pro fulfilment independent of the first.

- The Pro checkout now stamps `userId` and `campaignId` onto the subscription itself (`subscription_data.metadata`), so the Stripe object names its account without the checkout session, which Stripe does not keep forever.
- `customer.subscription.created` fulfils from that stamp: resolve the account from `metadata.userId`, link the campaign, and flip `isPro` when the subscription is billing (`active`/`trialing`).

Three guards keep the second arm from reintroducing the failures the first one had:

- A campaign already holding a **different** `subscriptionId` is left untouched. Re-linking it orphans the subscription that is still billing, which is the ENG-11084 mechanism the repair script exists to undo; it error-logs the duplicate signature instead.
- A subscription with **no** `metadata.userId` keeps today's behaviour exactly: linked by the stored Stripe customer id, no entitlement. It cannot prove which campaign it was sold for.
- `past_due`, `unpaid`, `incomplete` and `canceled` are linked but never fulfil, so an abandoned checkout does not become Pro. Linking them matters because their later `updated`/`deleted` events resolve through that id.

The completion path is unchanged and neither arm depends on the other: whichever arrives second is a no-op on the campaign, because `setIsPro` reports `becamePro` only on the genuine non-Pro to Pro transition, and the one-time upgrade side effects are gated on it. Stripe delivers the two events concurrently, so both orderings are covered by a route test.

Deliberately out of scope, per the analysis:

- **P2 alerting.** Time-to-detect only; the point of this PR is that there is nothing left to detect.
- **P3 reconcile (pg-boss schedule).** Heals drift after the fact and needs prod Stripe credentials on every run. `packages/gp-api/src/cron` is deleted and CI-banned, so if it lands it lands in `jobs.registry.ts`.
- **Backfilling metadata onto existing subscriptions**, and repairing the accumulated pre-2026-09-17 drift. Those rows are already billed and their campaigns already wrong; that is a data repair against a reviewed list, not a code path.
- ENG-11454 (orphan-sibling cancel) and branch `fix/ENG-11454-pro-cancel` are untouched.

Docs: `docs/adr/2026-11-18-pro-fulfilment-two-arms-and-subscription-metadata.md` records the decision, and `packages/gp-api/src/payments/AGENTS.md` no longer claims `userId` is never written onto the subscription.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes Pro entitlement and subscription-to-campaign linking in payment webhooks; mistakes could double-grant Pro, skip upgrades, or mishandle duplicate subscriptions.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a **second Pro fulfilment arm** so a missed `checkout.session.completed` no longer leaves a paying account on the free plan. Pro checkout now writes **`userId` and `campaignId` onto the Stripe subscription** (`subscription_data.metadata`), and **`customer.subscription.created`** can link `details.subscriptionId` and call **`setIsPro`** when the subscription is **`active` or `trialing`** and carries the checkout stamp.
> 
> **Guards:** campaigns already linked to a **different** subscription are left alone (error log only); subscriptions **without** stamped metadata still link by customer id but do not grant Pro; **non-billing** statuses are linked only, not fulfilled. The existing completion path is unchanged—whichever sibling event arrives second is idempotent via `becamePro`.
> 
> **Checkout API:** `PurchaseController` / `StripeService` Pro session creation now takes **`campaignId`** so metadata is set at session creation. Docs (ADR + `AGENTS.md`) and route/unit tests cover the new path and race ordering.
>

@@ -0,0 +1,57 @@
+---
+title: Pro fulfilment has two webhook arms, and the subscription carries its own account link
+status: active
+decided_by: [agent]
+date: 2026-11-18
+code: ['#3876']
+scope:
+  - packages/gp-api/src/payments/**
+  - packages/gp-api/src/vendors/stripe/**
+---
+
+# Pro fulfilment has two webhook arms, and the subscription carries its own account link
+
+## Decision
+
+A Pro subscription is fulfilled by either `checkout.session.completed` or
+`customer.subscription.created`, whichever arrives first, and the Pro checkout
+stamps `userId` and `campaignId` onto the subscription itself
+(`subscription_data.metadata`) so the Stripe object names its account without
+the checkout session.
+
+## Context
+
+`campaign.details.subscriptionId` is the only mapping from a live subscription
+back to an account, and one webhook wrote it: a missed, delayed or lost
+`checkout.session.completed` left a paying account on the free plan with no
+retry, no local record of what to retry, and a customer who could only be
+released by a human cancelling in Stripe. The 2026-11-17 root-cause analysis
+(ENG-11182, ENG-11672) found the class ticket's cases were exactly that shape.
+
+Stripe delivers a subscription's sibling events independently, so the two
+events are already a race today; only one of them was allowed to win it. The
+`created` event carries the subscription, and the checkout session is a
+separate object that Stripe retains for a limited time, so putting the ids on
+the subscription is the only way to make the link durable.
+
+## Alternatives rejected
+
+- **Keep one fulfilment path and add a reconcile job.** A pg-boss schedule
+  comparing Stripe against the campaign rows heals drift, but only after the
+  candidate has been on the free plan for a cycle, and it needs prod Stripe
+  credentials on every run. It repairs; it does not prevent.
+- **Alert only.** Detection shortens time-to-detect and leaves the manual
+  cancellation in place.
+- **Backfill metadata onto existing subscriptions.** Not needed to stop
+  recurrence (new subscriptions carry it), and it puts a write on every live
+  subscription for no entitlement change; the accumulated drift is a data
+  repair, tracked separately.
+- **Trust the Stripe customer id for fulfilment.** A customer can hold several
+  subscriptions and pre-ENG-11084 checkouts minted a customer per session, so a
+  customer match does not identify the campaign that was sold.
+
+## Revisit if
+
+Stripe stops delivering `customer.subscription.created`, or the webhook
+endpoint's subscribed event list drops it: the second arm is silent without it,
+and nothing in CI checks the dashboard's list.

diff --git a/packages/gp-api/src/payments/paymentEvents.subscriptionCreated.routes.test.ts b/packages/gp-api/src/payments/paymentEvents.subscriptionCreated.routes.test.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..9459dc3bc8
--- /dev/null
+++ b/packages/gp-api/src/payments/paymentEvents.subscriptionCreated.routes.test.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,395 @@
+import { CrmCampaignsService } from '@/campaigns/services/crmCampaigns.service'
+import { RaceOpponentService } from '@/raceOpponent/services/raceOpponent.service'
+import { useTestService } from '@/test-service'
+import { SlackService } from '@/vendors/slack/services/slack.service'
+import { addDays, format } from 'date-fns'
+import Stripe from 'stripe'
+import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest'
+import { CheckoutSessionMode, WebhookEventType } from './payments.types'
+
+// Route-level coverage for Pro fulfilment from `customer.subscription.created`.
+// `checkout.session.completed` used to be the only path that stored
+// `details.subscriptionId` and flipped `isPro`, so a completion that was
+// missed, delayed or lost left a paying account on the free plan with nothing
+// to retry (ENG-11182, ENG-11672). A Pro checkout now stamps `userId` and
+// `campaignId` onto the subscription itself, and this event can fulfil from
+// that stamp, so the two sibling events are independent arms of one outcome
+// rather than one arm and one formality.
+//
+// Delivered through the real `POST /v1/payments/events` controller against a
+// real Postgres, for the same reason as the cancellation suite: the effects
+// under test are rows in the campaign, and the signature can be generated with
+// the same secret the app verifies against, so the event goes through
+// parse -> dispatch -> handler -> DB for real.
+
+const service = useTestService()
+
+const WEBHOOK_ROUTE = '/v1/payments/events'
+
+// Signing-only client. `generateTestHeaderString` is a local HMAC over the
+// payload, the same computation Stripe performs before delivery and
+// `StripeService.parseWebhookEvent` verifies on arrival, so no network call is
+// made and no live Stripe object is touched.
+const signer = new Stripe('sk_test_signing_only')
+
+const deliverStripeEvent = (event: Record<string, unknown>) => {
+  const payload = JSON.stringify(event)
+  return service.client.post(WEBHOOK_ROUTE, payload, {
+    headers: {
+      'content-type': 'application/json',
+      'stripe-signature': signer.webhooks.generateTestHeaderString({
+        payload,
+        secret: process.env.STRIPE_WEBSOCKET_SECRET as string,
+      }),
+    },
+  })
+}
+
+const nowInSeconds = () => Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000)
+
+let eventSeq = 0
+
+const eventEnvelope = (type: string, object: Record<string, unknown>) => {
+  eventSeq += 1
+  return {
+    id: `evt_test_pro_fulfilment_${eventSeq}`,
+    object: 'event',
+    api_version: '2025-03-31.basil',
+    created: nowInSeconds(),
+    livemode: false,
+    pending_webhooks: 0,
+    request: { id: null, idempotency_key: null },
+    type,
+    data: { object },
+  }
+}
+
+type SubscriptionCreatedOptions = {
+  subscriptionId: string
+  customerId: string
+  status: Stripe.Subscription.Status
+  // Absent on a subscription minted before the checkout stamped it, or by
+  // anything that is not our Pro checkout.
+  metadata?: Record<string, string>
+}
+
+const subscriptionCreatedEvent = ({
+  subscriptionId,
+  customerId,
+  status,
+  metadata,
+}: SubscriptionCreatedOptions) =>
+  eventEnvelope(WebhookEventType.CustomerSubscriptionCreated, {
+    id: subscriptionId,
+    object: 'subscription',
+    customer: customerId,
+    currency: 'usd',
+    status,
+    canceled_at: null,
+    cancel_at: null,
+    cancel_at_period_end: false,
+    cancellation_details: null,
+    items: { object: 'list', data: [], has_more: false, url: '' },
+    ...(metadata ? { metadata } : {}),
+  })
+
+const checkoutCompletedEvent = ({
+  subscriptionId,
+  customerId,
+  userId,
+}: {
+  subscriptionId: string
+  customerId: string
+  userId: number
+}) =>
+  eventEnvelope(WebhookEventType.CheckoutSessionCompleted, {
+    id: 'cs_test_pro',
+    object: 'checkout.session',
+    mode: CheckoutSessionMode.SUBSCRIPTION,
+    customer: customerId,
+    subscription: subscriptionId,
+    payment_status: 'paid',
+    metadata: { userId: String(userId) },
+  })
+
+let campaignSeq = 0
+
+// A campaign that passes `isActiveCampaign`, i.e. one the Pro checkout would
+// have sold to: an upcoming election date and no recorded result.
+const seedCampaign = async (details: Record<string, unknown> = {}) => {
+  campaignSeq += 1
+  const slug = `pro-fulfilment-${campaignSeq}`
+  await service.prisma.organization.create({
+    data: { slug, ownerId: service.user.id },
+  })
+  return service.prisma.campaign.create({
+    data: {
+      slug,
+      organizationSlug: slug,
+      userId: service.user.id,
+      details: {
+        electionDate: format(addDays(new Date(), 30), 'yyyy-MM-dd'),
+        ...details,
+      },
+    },
+  })
+}
+
+const readCampaign = (id: number) =>
+  service.prisma.campaign.findUniqueOrThrow({ where: { id } })
+
+// The dispatch is one of the one-time Pro-upgrade side effects, gated on the
+// same `becamePro` transition as the flip. Only the arm that wins the race can
+// fire it, so the arm that loses must not be the only one that knows about it.
+const spyOnOpponentCollection = () =>
+  vi
+    .spyOn(service.app.get(RaceOpponentService), 'autoCollectOnProUpgrade')
+    .mockResolvedValue(undefined)
+
+beforeEach(() => {
+  // `setIsPro` ends in a CRM sync and `checkout.session.completed` in two
+  // candidate-facing notifications. Both are third-party calls incidental to
+  // the rows under test, and the harness carries tokens for neither.
+  vi.spyOn(
+    service.app.get(CrmCampaignsService),
+    'trackCampaign',
+  ).mockResolvedValue(undefined)
+  vi.spyOn(service.app.get(SlackService), 'message').mockResolvedValue(
+    undefined,
+  )
+})
+
+describe('POST /v1/payments/events — customer.subscription.created', () => {
+  // ENG-11672: the account is billed on a live subscription while the
+  // dashboard says free. Both halves matter — the link is what makes every
+  // later subscription event resolvable, and the flip is what the candidate
+  // sees — so they are asserted as one outcome.
+  it('links the campaign and flips it Pro for an active subscription', async () => {
+    const campaign = await seedCampaign()
+    const opponentCollection = spyOnOpponentCollection()
+
+    const res = await deliverStripeEvent(
+      subscriptionCreatedEvent({
+        subscriptionId: 'sub_pro_created',
+        customerId: 'cus_pro_created',
+        status: 'active',
+        metadata: {
+          userId: String(service.user.id),
+          campaignId: String(campaign.id),
+        },
+      }),
+    )
+
+    expect(res.status).toBe(200)
+
+    const updated = await readCampaign(campaign.id)
+    expect(updated.details.subscriptionId).toBe('sub_pro_created')
+    expect(updated.isPro).toBe(true)
+    expect(updated.details.isProUpdatedAt).toBeDefined()
+    // Flipping Pro without this leaves the candidate Pro with no opponent
+    // research started, because the sibling completion event then computes
+    // `becamePro === false` and skips its own dispatch.
+    expect(opponentCollection).toHaveBeenCalledExactlyOnceWith(campaign.id)
+  })
+
+  it('flips Pro for a trialing subscription', async () => {
+    const campaign = await seedCampaign()
+
+    const res = await deliverStripeEvent(
+      subscriptionCreatedEvent({
+        subscriptionId: 'sub_pro_trialing',
+        customerId: 'cus_pro_trialing',
+        status: 'trialing',
+        metadata: { userId: String(service.user.id) },
+      }),
+    )
+
+    expect(res.status).toBe(200)
+    expect((await readCampaign(campaign.id)).isPro).toBe(true)
+  })
+
+  // The link and the entitlement are separate decisions. A subscription that
+  // has not been paid for is still worth storing — its later `updated` and
+  // `deleted` events resolve through that id, and an `incomplete` one can
+  // become active without a second `created` — but handing out Pro for it
+  // would give the product away to every abandoned checkout.
+  it.each<Stripe.Subscription.Status>([
+    'incomplete',
+    'past_due',
+    'unpaid',
+    'canceled',
+  ])('links a %s subscription without flipping Pro', async (status) => {
+    const campaign = await seedCampaign()
+    const opponentCollection = spyOnOpponentCollection()
+
+    const res = await deliverStripeEvent(
+      subscriptionCreatedEvent({
+        subscriptionId: `sub_pro_${status}`,
+        customerId: `cus_pro_${status}`,
+        status,
+        metadata: { userId: String(service.user.id) },
+      }),
+    )
+
+    expect(res.status).toBe(200)
+
+    const updated = await readCampaign(campaign.id)
+    expect(updated.details.subscriptionId).toBe(`sub_pro_${status}`)
+    expect(updated.isPro).toBe(false)
+    expect(opponentCollection).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
+  })
+
+  // Overwriting a different stored id is the duplicate-checkout shape
+  // (ENG-11084): the subscription that was carrying the campaign keeps billing
+  // with nothing pointing at it. The replay-safe direction is to leave the row
+  // exactly as it was, which also means no second Pro claim.
+  it('leaves a campaign that already holds a different subscriptionId untouched', async () => {
+    const upgradedAt = '2026-01-15T00:00:00Z'
+    const campaign = await seedCampaign({
+      subscriptionId: 'sub_already_linked',
+      isProUpdatedAt: upgradedAt,
+    })
+
+    const res = await deliverStripeEvent(
+      subscriptionCreatedEvent({
+        subscriptionId: 'sub_second_checkout',
+        customerId: 'cus_second_checkout',
+        status: 'active',
+        metadata: { userId: String(service.user.id) },
+      }),
+    )
+
+    expect(res.status).toBe(200)
+
+    const updated = await readCampaign(campaign.id)
+    expect(updated.details.subscriptionId).toBe('sub_already_linked')
+    expect(updated.isPro).toBe(false)
+    expect(updated.details.isProUpdatedAt).toBe(upgradedAt)
+  })
+
+  // A subscription nobody stamped at checkout proves which customer it belongs
+  // to but not which campaign it was sold for, so it keeps the pre-existing
+  // behaviour: linked by customer id, no entitlement granted.
+  it('links by customer id without flipping Pro when the subscription carries no metadata', async () => {
+    const campaign = await seedCampaign()
+    await service.prisma.user.update({
+      where: { id: service.user.id },
+      data: { metaData: { customerId: 'cus_unstamped' } },
+    })
+
+    const res = await deliverStripeEvent(
+      subscriptionCreatedEvent({
+        subscriptionId: 'sub_unstamped',
+        customerId: 'cus_unstamped',
+        status: 'active',
+      }),
+    )
+
+    expect(res.status).toBe(200)
+
+    const updated = await readCampaign(campaign.id)
+    expect(updated.details.subscriptionId).toBe('sub_unstamped')
+    expect(updated.isPro).toBe(false)
+  })
+})
+
+describe('POST /v1/payments/events — checkout.session.completed (regression)', () => {
+  it('still fulfils Pro and stamps the upgrade once', async () => {
+    const campaign = await seedCampaign()
+
+    const res = await deliverStripeEvent(
+      checkoutCompletedEvent({
+        subscriptionId: 'sub_checkout_completed',
+        customerId: 'cus_checkout_completed',
+        userId: service.user.id,
+      }),
+    )
+
+    expect(res.status).toBe(200)
+
+    const updated = await readCampaign(campaign.id)
+    expect(updated.details.subscriptionId).toBe('sub_checkout_completed')
+    expect(updated.isPro).toBe(true)
+    expect(updated.details.isProUpdatedAt).toBeDefined()
+  })
+
+  // Stripe delivers the two sibling events concurrently and in either order.
+  // Whichever lands second must be a no-op on the campaign: the same id is
+  // re-written (a merged jsonb patch, so no clobbering), and `becamePro` is
+  // what gates the one-time upgrade side effects, so a second delivery cannot
+  // announce or stamp the upgrade again.
+  it('is a no-op on a campaign the created event already fulfilled', async () => {
+    const campaign = await seedCampaign()
+    const opponentCollection = spyOnOpponentCollection()
+
+    await deliverStripeEvent(
+      subscriptionCreatedEvent({
+        subscriptionId: 'sub_racing',
+        customerId: 'cus_racing',
+        status: 'active',
+        metadata: { userId: String(service.user.id) },
+      }),
+    )
+    const afterCreated = await readCampaign(campaign.id)
+    expect(afterCreated.isPro).toBe(true)
+
+    const res = await deliverStripeEvent(
+      checkoutCompletedEvent({
+        subscriptionId: 'sub_racing',
+        customerId: 'cus_racing',
+        userId: service.user.id,
+      }),
+    )
+
+    expect(res.status).toBe(200)
+
+    const afterCompleted = await readCampaign(campaign.id)
+    expect(afterCompleted.details.subscriptionId).toBe('sub_racing')
+    expect(afterCompleted.isPro).toBe(true)
+    expect(afterCompleted.details.isProUpdatedAt).toBe(
+      afterCreated.details.isProUpdatedAt,
+    )
+    expect(opponentCollection).toHaveBeenCalledExactlyOnceWith(campaign.id)
+  })
+
+  // The reverse order: Stripe delivers the two sibling events concurrently, so
+  // `completed` can be the arm that fulfils. The `created` event that follows
+  // finds the id already stored and the campaign already Pro, and must change
+  // nothing — no second flip, no second stamp, no second one-time dispatch.
+  it('is a no-op when the created event arrives after the completion', async () => {
+    const campaign = await seedCampaign()
+    const opponentCollection = spyOnOpponentCollection()
+
+    await deliverStripeEvent(
+      checkoutCompletedEvent({
+        subscriptionId: 'sub_completed_first',
+        customerId: 'cus_completed_first',
+        userId: service.user.id,
+      }),
+    )
+    const afterCompleted = await readCampaign(campaign.id)
+    expect(afterCompleted.isPro).toBe(true)
+
+    const res = await deliverStripeEvent(
+      subscriptionCreatedEvent({
+        subscriptionId: 'sub_completed_first',
+        customerId: 'cus_completed_first',
+        status: 'active',
+        metadata: {
+          userId: String(service.user.id),
+          campaignId: String(campaign.id),
+        },
+      }),
+    )
+
+    expect(res.status).toBe(200)
+
+    const afterCreated = await readCampaign(campaign.id)
+    expect(afterCreated.details.subscriptionId).toBe('sub_completed_first')
+    expect(afterCreated.isPro).toBe(true)
+    expect(afterCreated.details.isProUpdatedAt).toBe(
+      afterCompleted.details.isProUpdatedAt,
+    )
+    expect(opponentCollection).toHaveBeenCalledExactlyOnceWith(campaign.id)
+  })
+})
